grades.main_gap: Lemma 1 (only finitely many primes appear; hitting sets stabilize) is the crux and is unproven: the greedy pairwise-disjoint subsequence claim is false, and the promised rigorous pigeonhole argument never appears; backward propagation to all n is also merely asserted.
grades.notes: The hitting-set reformulation and Step 2 (tail = increasing merge of finitely many APs with moduli dividing L, giving T=|R|, shift L) are essentially sound conditional on stabilization. But the 'Key Observation' is false (extra primes can appear, e.g. 42=2·3·7 in the write-up's own example), and Step 1's proof collapses into hand-waving.
